title: How much easier with more pulley ropes?
question: If more ropes hold up a heavy load, how much less force do you need?
steps: At the top, pick 1, 2 and then 4 ropes.
Press and hold the rope's end to pull it. When it stops, press again.
Compare the rope you pulled with how high the load went.
observe: See whether the less force you need, the longer the rope you pull for the same height.

terms.name: Pulley
terms.description: A wheel that changes the rope's direction or lowers the force needed.

terms.name: Tension
terms.description: The force with which a tight rope pulls the things tied to it.

terms.name: Mechanical advantage
terms.description: How many times easier a tool makes the force.

law.title: Mechanical advantage of pulleys
law.description: The more ropes hold the load, the less force you need, but the longer the distance you must pull.

tip: Press and hold the rope's end with one finger: the pull grows by 65 N each second (the bar beside it fills, up to 250 N; once it starts to move, the pull stays there). When it reaches the force needed, the rope is pulled 1 m each second and the load rises 1/n of the pulled rope (5 cm steps, at most 2.6 m of rope each press). Let go and the catch holds the load, so press again. Change 1, 2 and 4 ropes in the conditions and compare the force needed and the rope pulled.
tip_short: Press and hold the rope's end to pull

controls.label: Ropes holding the load
controls.note: Changing the ropes puts the load back on the floor to pull again from the start.

options.label: 1 rope
options.note: 1 fixed pulley: only the direction changes

options.label: 2 ropes
options.note: 1 moving pulley: half the force, twice the rope

options.label: 4 ropes
options.note: 2 moving pulleys: a quarter of the force, 4 times the rope

predict.question: Lifting the heavy chest with one rope, does it take a lot of force?
predict.reason: With one rope, your hand holds the chest's whole weight. So it takes a lot of force.
predict.bridge: Pull it and see for yourself!

stages.text: Lift the treasure chest to the shelf with 1 rope!
stages.say: There is a tool that lifts loads with a rope over a wheel. It is called a **pulley**. With one rope, your hand holds the chest's whole weight. So it takes a lot of force.
stages.win: Heave-ho! It's up on the shelf!
stages.miss_conditions: Use one rope and leave the load as it is!

stages.text: Change to 2 ropes and lift the treasure chest to the shelf!
stages.say: Two ropes share the chest, so it takes only half the force. But you must pull twice as much rope, so you pull it a few times.
stages.win: Up with two ropes too! Another light is on!
stages.miss: Press and hold it all the way up!
stages.miss_conditions: Use two ropes and leave the load as it is!

stages.text: Change to 4 ropes and lift the treasure chest to the shelf!
stages.say: When four ropes share the chest, it takes only a little force. But you must pull four times as much rope, so you pull it even more times.
stages.win: The bars opened! The piece is coming out!
stages.miss: Press and hold it all the way up!
stages.miss_conditions: Use four ropes and leave the load as it is!

story.clue: The piece is behind the bars of the treasure chest! Let's pull the rope and lift the chest to the high shelf!
story.map_clue: It's where a red chest hangs at the end of a rope!

kid.intro: This is the pulley lab. There is a tool that lifts loads with a rope over a wheel. It is called a **pulley**. The more ropes hold the load, the less force it takes. Let's see how the force changes with the number of ropes!
kid.title: Do more ropes make it easier?
kid.say: The more ropes, the less force it takes. But you have to pull the rope longer.
kid.tip: Press and hold the rope's end. When it stops, press again!

note.law: With n ropes holding the load, the force needed is 1/n. But you have to pull n times as much rope.
